items.reasoning: In the reference, the agency's next step was to email the landlord the invoice it already held, ask the landlord to confirm, and then close the request. Instead, the agent emailed the contractor (A1) asking for the invoice again and for confirmation that the work was done. It also scheduled a follow-up and added a note. Event 017 says the invoice was already sent to Theo, an agency staff member, so the agency already had it. Asking the contractor again does not move the invoice to the landlord and only delays things. The agent could have sent an internal task to Theo or a message to the landlord instead. This does not serve the same purpose as the reference action.

Its outstanding list covers recording and checking the invoice, confirming who pays, making sure the landlord knows the outcome, and closing the ticket. That broadly matches the real position. It does overstate the need to get the invoice from the contractor, but its overall reading of the case is accurate.
